tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

schema.name: SearchPlugins
schema.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

keywords.description: Keyword phrases describing the user's intent.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

## meshy

# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
If the user hasn't said what the model is for (a game asset, a character to rig, a render, a 3D print, AR), ask before you pick models (Rule 4). A game asset or a face-count budget means smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2 with target_polycount), also on meshy_text_to_3d; never a meshy-7.1 model remeshed down.
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one; on meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d also the texture_model, suggesting a pair from "Choosing Models" below), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k"); retexture meshy-n1 10 (2K only) |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | 20 (texture_model meshy-7 only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

texture_model never changes the price; 4K/8K need the meshy-7 or meshy-6 texture model. Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Choosing Models (meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d)
Choose models by project (geometry ai_model + texture_model):
- Detailed hero asset, product render, cinematic prop: meshy-7.1 + meshy-7 (PBR, up to 8K)
- Game character to rig and animate: meshy-t2.5 (smart topology, set target_polycount) + meshy-n1
- Many props for a game scene, or user-generated content: meshy-t2 (smart topology) + meshy-n1
- A real object from 2 to 4 photos: meshy-7.1 on Multi-Image to 3D + meshy-7
- A model to 3D print: meshy-7.1 + none, or meshy-7 to print in color
- Many drafts at a low cost: meshy-6-lite + meshy-6-lite
More: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/models
Omit texture_model for the geometry's default; "none" is should_texture false; smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2) is single-image only. A texture model refuses options it cannot do (e.g. meshy-n1: no texture_prompt, enable_pbr or 4K); the tool says so before any charge.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the ta… [truncated]

content.text: Plan shown (5 steps).

content.content:
1	# Handoff: la escopeta (Glyphbound), con el mismo proceso que el rifle
2	
3	**Para:** un chat nuevo de Claude Code en `C:\GameJam` (máquina CENTRAL).
4	**De:** el chat que rehízo el rifle el 2026-11-12 (bloques 18 a 23 y 25 de `Devlog/days/2026-11-12.md`).
5	**Antes de nada:** lee `CLAUDE.md`, `Devlog/README.md` y esos bloques de la bitácora: son la historia completa de lo que aquí se resume.
6	
7	## El encargo
8	El dueño quiere para la escopeta lo mismo que se hizo con el rifle: un arma 3D en primera persona que se vea sólida y limpia, completa y funcional (gatillo, recarga animada, barra de energía, holograma de munición, luz de punto débil, fogonazo y retroceso), al nivel de la pistola y del rifle, que ya aprobó.
9	
10	## Qué hay hoy
11	- **Datos:** la escopeta existe en `Glyphbound/Content/Data/Weapons.json` (`"Id": "Shotgun"`): 8 perdigones de 10, un disparo cada 0,8 s, 6 cartuchos, 4 cargadores de reserva, recarga de 2 s. **No tiene `"ViewModel"`**, así que en el juego se ve con formas provisionales.
12	- **Arte:** no hay nada de la escopeta en `Glyphbound/SourceArt/Weapons/` ni en `/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/`.
13	  - En `C:\Users\VNasher\Downloads` hay un zip de Tripo reciente sin identificar (`tripo_convert_8f45a6e1-....zip`, del 12 nov 22:01: un FBX de 0,7 MB y una sola textura). **No sé si es la escopeta.** Pregunta al dueño cuál es el archivo fuente antes de abrir nada.
14	- **Código:** las dos armas reales comparten un solo camino en `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Weapons/GBGun.cpp`, descrito por una tabla de arte por modelo (`FGBGunModelArt`, constantes `PistolArt` y `RifleArt`, y la lista de `FindModelArt`). Añadir un tercer modelo es una constante nueva más una entrada en esa lista, **si el arma encaja en el contrato de abajo**.
15	
16	## Contrato que el código espera de un modelo
17	**Mallas en `/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/<Arma>/`**, todas obligatorias salvo la barra: si falta una, el juego avisa y vuelve a las formas provisionales.
18	- `SM_<Arma>_Body`: todo lo que no se mueve.
19	- `SM_<Arma>_Trigger`: origen en su bisagra.
20	- `SM_<Arma>_Magazine`: origen en su posición de reposo.
21	- `SM_<Arma>_WeakPointLight`: lo que se enciende al acertar en punto débil.
22	- `SM_<Arma>_AmmoDisplay`: un panel 2:1 mirando al jugador; U hacia la derecha del jugador.
23	- `SM_<Arma>_EnergyBar`: solo si la barra es una malla aparte (pistola). En el rifle va dentro del material del cuerpo.
24	
25	**Ejes y unidades:** cañón hacia +X, origen del cuerpo en el punto de la mano (arriba de la empuñadura), 1 unidad = 1 cm.
26	
27	**Parámetros de material que pone el juego** en todas las piezas: `ElementColor`; además `ImbueRemaining` (barra de energía de 13 celdas, según el UV 1), `Flash` (luz de punto débil) y `DisplayTexture` (holograma).
28	
29	**El holograma lo dibuja el juego** si el modelo pone `bDrawDisplayFrame` (rifle): líneas de marco, número y un punto por bala. Con 6 cartuchos saldrán 6 puntos.
30	
31	## Dos decisiones de diseño que la escopeta obliga a tomar
32	Son del arquitecto, pero cambian cómo se ve el arma, así que cuéntaselas al dueño en una sola pregunta y sigue con un valor provisional mientras responde.
33	1. **Recarga.** El código actual es de cargador: saca uno, mete otro y las balas llegan al final (`FinishReload`). Una escopeta clásica se carga cartucho a cartucho por un tubo.
34	   - Lo que no cuesta código: una escopeta de cargador de caja, que reutiliza la animación de recarga tal cual.
35	   - Lo que sí cuesta: cartucho a cartucho. Cambia la lógica de munición (recarga parcial, interrumpible) y la animación.
36	2. **Corredera.** Con 0,8 s entre disparos, lo natural es una corredera que va y vuelve tras cada tiro. Es una pieza móvil nueva (`SM_<Arma>_Pump`) y un movimiento nuevo en `UpdateViewModel`; el contrato de hoy no la tiene.
37	
38	## El proceso que funcionó con el rifle
39	1. **Inspecciona la fuente antes de tocarla.** Ábrela en Blender sin interfaz y mira triángulos, piezas sueltas, piezas tras soldar vértices, texturas y mapas que trae.
40	   - El GLB del rifle era una exportación de pocos polígonos (5.498 triángulos) con una sola textura de color con luz horneada y manchas, sin rugosidad, metálico, normales ni oclusión. Esa era la causa de que se viera "de gelatina", no los ajustes en Unreal.
41	   - Si la fuente de la escopeta es igual de pobre, dilo pronto: pedir a Tripo una exportación con más detalle y texturas PBR sale más barato que reconstruir. **No gastes créditos de Tripo, Meshy ni Hyper3D sin permiso.**
42	2. **Renderiza la fuente tal cual desde la cámara del jugador** y míralo tú antes que nadie. `Tools/Blender/rifle_render_review.py` hace las vistas (primera persona, primeros planos y ortográficas a escala para medir); las posiciones de cámara son las del rifle, cópialo y adáptalo.
43	3. **Reconstruye el aspecto con un script**, no a mano: `Tools/Blender/rifle_build_blend.py` es la plantilla (GLB → `Rifle.blend`, unos 4 minutos). Lo que hace:
44	   - suelda vértices, tira las normales de Tripo, marca aristas duras y recalcula normales por área de cara;
45	   - pone un tono plano por panel (mediana de brillo ajustada a una paleta: polímero blanco, dos grises, metal oscuro) y recorta nítidos los detalles pequeños dibujados;
46	   - hornea en Cycles la oclusión y un mapa de normales con aristas redondeadas;
47	   - fuerza piezas enteras a un tono cuando sus paneles no coinciden, y limpia manchas por posición en el arma (cada téxel sabe dónde está);
48	   - modela lo que la fuente trae roto o no trae: en el rifle, el riel, las barras de energía, los paneles laterales, el emisor del holograma y el cargador.
49	4. **Mide antes de modelar.** Los mapas de profundidad con rayos (BVH de Blender, un rayo cada 5 mm) dieron el plano exacto de cada cara y localizaron un surco que a ojo se leía como "roto".
50	5. **Enseña renders y espera el visto bueno antes de importar** (regla del dueño). Con el rifle hubo cuatro rondas de notas sobre renders antes del "sí, impórtalo". Dos lecciones:
51	   - los renders deben ser desde el punto de vista del jugador: el dueño lo dijo expresamente;
52	   - el render tiene que mostrar lo que mostrará el juego. El holograma se dibujó opaco en el render cuando en el juego era translúcido, y el dueño pidió arreglar algo que el juego no habría enseñado.
53	6. **Exporta sin reconstruir mallas.** `Tools/Blender/rifle_export_fbx.py` copia cada objeto del `.blend` y lo mueve; un paso por bmesh pierde las normales propias y el arma vuelve a verse blanda. Los pivotes van como propiedades de los objetos.
54	7. **Importa** con el Editor cerrado: `Tools/Jam/Import-Rifle.ps1` y `Tools/Jam/import_rifle.py` son la plantilla (texturas, materiales construidos por script, comprobaciones de ranuras y del UV de la barra).

1	# Jam dev log (goal: the Glass Box prize for the best dev log)
2	
3	Everything any agent or person does on the project must be recorded here. If it is not in the dev log, it did not happen as far as the judges are concerned.
4	
5	**Language:** the Official Rules (7(i)) require every part of the submission in English, and that includes the published dev log. Write `days/*.md`, `media/` captions and `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` in English. Raw logs (`raw/`) and the team's prompts to agents can be in any language. When a day entry quotes a prompt written in Spanish, include the original and an English translation.
6	
7	## Layout
8	
9	```
10	Devlog/
11	  README.md                  this file (the rules)
12	  TEMPLATE_DAY.md            template for the daily entry
13	  PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md     what was prepared BEFORE Nov 12 (the jam requires declaring it)
14	  PREJAM_PREP.md             full pre-jam log: timeline, tests, tools evaluated, rules read
15	  raw/<MACHINE>/             raw automatic logs (NEVER published as they are)
16	    <YYYY-MM-DD>/claude-<session>.jsonl      every Claude Code event (hook)
17	    <YYYY-MM-DD>/transcripts/<session>.jsonl full transcript of each session
18	    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents.jsonl                every run of an external agent
19	    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents/<run>/               prompt, full output and diffstat of that run
20	    unreal/<log>.jsonl                       agent actions inside the Editor (MCP, Assistant, Canvas)
21	  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>_DRAFT.md                 automatic draft (already redacted)
22	  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md                       final entry for the day, written by a person (in English)
23	  media/<YYYY-MM-DD>/                        screenshots, gifs and clips of the day
24	```
25	
26	## Rules for everyone (people and agents)
27	
28	1. **Claude Code** is logged automatically by the **user-level** hooks that `Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` installs on each machine. They log every session opened in the jam root or any subfolder (the root is the folder that contains `Devlog/.jamroot`). Do not disable them and do not delete `.jamroot`.
29	2. **Any other agent** (Codex, cursor-agent, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Gemini, generation scripts) is ALWAYS launched with:
30	   `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent <name> -Model <model> -PromptFile <prompt.md> -Purpose "<what for>" -Command '<command>'`
31	   - Use `-Shell cmd` if the command contains `< file`.
32	   - That is what records it. An agent launched by hand leaves no record.
33	   - **Cursor** (the art LAPTOP, which has no repo) is logged by user-level Cursor hooks instead: `Tools/Devlog/Install-CursorHooks.ps1` installs `cursor-devlog-hook.ps1`, which writes `C:\JamLog\raw\<MACHINE>\<date>\cursor-<conversation>.jsonl` (plus transcripts). `Register-LaptopDevlogTasks.ps1` copies that folder every 10 minutes to `Incoming\LAPTOP\_devlog_raw` on CENTRAL, and CENTRAL's `JamDevlogImport` task (`Import-RemoteDevlog.ps1`) moves it into `Devlog/raw/`, where `New-DevlogDay.ps1` reads it. The same kit runs on ASSETS (destination `Incoming\ASSETS\_devlog_raw`).
34	   - **Codex chats** (desktop app, IDE extension or interactive CLI, i.e. anything not launched through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`) on machines without the repo: before each sync, `Collect-CodexSessions.ps1` copies the session files Codex keeps in `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\sessions` (full prompts, replies and tool calls) into `C:\JamLog\raw\<MACHINE>\<date>\codex-*.jsonl`. `New-DevlogDay.ps1` reads those too.
35	   - **Cursor transcripts:** `Collect-CursorTranscripts.ps1` also copies the full agent transcripts Cursor keeps in `%USERPROFILE%.cursorprojects*gent-transcripts`, so chats from before the hook was installed are not lost. The draft takes Cursor prompts from the transcript whenever there is one (it is complete; the hook missed some prompts before the mutex fix).
36	   - **Claude Code and Gemini CLI** on machines without the repo: `Collect-OtherAgents.ps1` copies their session files (`%USERPROFILE%.claudeprojects`, `%USERPROFILE%.gemini	mp`). OpenCode keeps its sessions in a SQLite database, so it is always launched through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`; on ASSETS the sync also sends that repo's `Devlogaw` (`-ExtraSource`).
37	   - **Size:** every collector strips base64 images (screenshots, renders) from the copies (`JamLogCopy.ps1`): one Codex session on ASSETS went from 110 MB to 4.2 MB with every message and tool call intact. `Import-RemoteDevlog.ps1` refuses files over 50 MB and logs them, because `Devlog/raw` goes to GitHub, which rejects files over 100 MB.
38	   - On CENTRAL, Codex and OpenCode always run through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`, so this collection is only needed on machines without the repo.
39	3. **Prompts as files:** external agents get their prompt in a `.md` under `Prompts/`, never typed loose in the terminal.
40	4. **Web or desktop tools** (Fab, cloud Canvas, audio or image generators, Blender by hand): in the day entry, write down the tool, the prompt, the result and the final asset, and save a screenshot in `media/`.
41	5. **Unreal Editor:** always close it with `Tools/Jam/Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, which closes open asset editors first (an open animation editor crashes the Editor on exit) and collects the log. If it was closed some other way, or before deleting `Saved/`, run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Collect-UnrealAgentLog.ps1 -ProjectDir <folder of the .uproject>`.
42	6. **`JAM_MACHINE` variable:** each machine sets its own (`CENTRAL`, `ASSETS`…) so we know where each thing happened:
43	   `setx JAM_MACHINE CENTRAL`
44	7. **Small, frequent commits** with clear messages: the daily draft lists them. Commit `Devlog/raw/` too (the repo is private). Epic may ask for the version control history.
45	8. **End of day:** run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/New-DevlogDay.ps1 -Date <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Then a person writes `days/<date>.md` from `TEMPLATE_DAY.md`, starting from the draft.
46	9. **Publish:** only `days/*.md`, `media/`, `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` and `PREJAM_PREP.md`. Raw logs may contain keys or emails: the draft is already redacted, but check it before publishing. The dev log link goes in the submission, **before the deadline**.
47	10. **Times in UTC.** The jam ends on Nov 15 at 20:59 EST, which is **01:59 UTC on Nov 16**.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## meshy

# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
If the user hasn't said what the model is for (a game asset, a character to rig, a render, a 3D print, AR), ask before you pick models (Rule 4). A game asset or a face-count budget means smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2 with target_polycount), also on meshy_text_to_3d; never a meshy-7.1 model remeshed down.
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one; on meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d also the texture_model, suggesting a pair from "Choosing Models" below), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k"); retexture meshy-n1 10 (2K only) |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | 20 (texture_model meshy-7 only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

texture_model never changes the price; 4K/8K need the meshy-7 or meshy-6 texture model. Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Choosing Models (meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d)
Choose models by project (geometry ai_model + texture_model):
- Detailed hero asset, product render, cinematic prop: meshy-7.1 + meshy-7 (PBR, up to 8K)
- Game character to rig and animate: meshy-t2.5 (smart topology, set target_polycount) + meshy-n1
- Many props for a game scene, or user-generated content: meshy-t2 (smart topology) + meshy-n1
- A real object from 2 to 4 photos: meshy-7.1 on Multi-Image to 3D + meshy-7
- A model to 3D print: meshy-7.1 + none, or meshy-7 to print in color
- Many drafts at a low cost: meshy-6-lite + meshy-6-lite
More: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/models
Omit texture_model for the geometry's default; "none" is should_texture false; smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2) is single-image only. A texture model refuses options it cannot do (e.g. meshy-n1: no texture_prompt, enable_pbr or 4K); the tool says so before any charge.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the ta… [truncated]

Assets that arrive on CENTRAL (this machine) through the shared `Incoming` folders stop belonging there: they become part of the central project. Move the kept version into `Glyphbound/SourceArt/<Category>/<Asset>/` (outside git like `Content`; only its README with hashes is tracked) and delete the shared copies and older versions so no stale files pile up.

One copy per asset (owner, 2026-11-12, "solo necesitamos una pistola, no tengas en el proyecto mas de un asset de ella"): keep only the source file (e.g. `Pistol.blend`) and the Unreal assets. Intermediates (exported FBX, baked PNG) are made in a temporary folder by the import script and deleted after import (see `Tools/Jam/Import-Pistol.ps1`). No colour variants as separate files: use a material parameter.

**Why:** owner, 2026-11-12: shared folders are only for transit, and old versions and duplicate copies are clutter.
**How to apply:** for each incoming asset, verify the hash of the copy, write the README, delete the Incoming copy and work/review files; never leave exported intermediates next to the source. Mailbox messages (`_de_*`, `_para_*`) are not assets; leave them.

Before importing reworked 3D art into Unreal (meshes split, materials, holograms...), show the owner close-up renders and wait for approval.

**Why:** 2026-11-12, Entity (Tripo #26): I split and imported without asking; the owner found leftover tentacle bases (~5%) stuck on the body and said I should have asked first.

**How to apply:** render each part close up (e.g. each tentacle root individually), send them, ask; import only after the owner says yes. Related: [[assets-move-into-project]].

For first-person weapons, include renders from the player's camera. Owner, 2026-11-12, rifle: that viewpoint "is the right one because it is the one the player will have"; they judged shapes and stains from it over four rounds of notes.

The render must show what the game will show. Same day: my review render drew the additive ammo hologram as an opaque rectangle, and the owner asked to make it "more holographic", judging something the game would not have shown. (My reading: mimic the game material in the review render, or say what the render leaves out.)

metadata:

Assets that arrive on CENTRAL (this machine) through the shared `Incoming` folders stop belonging there: they become part of the central project. Move the kept version into `Glyphbound/SourceArt/<Category>/<Asset>/` (outside git like `Content`; only its README with hashes is tracked) and delete the shared copies and older versions so no stale files pile up.

One copy per asset (owner, 2026-11-12, "solo necesitamos una pistola, no tengas en el proyecto mas de un asset de ella"): keep only the source file (e.g. `Pistol.blend`) and the Unreal assets. Intermediates (exported FBX, baked PNG) are made in a temporary folder by the import script and deleted after import (see `Tools/Jam/Import-Pistol.ps1`). No colour variants as separate files: use a material parameter.

**Why:** owner, 2026-11-12: shared folders are only for transit, and old versions and duplicate copies are clutter.
**How to apply:** for each incoming asset, verify the hash of the copy, write the README, delete the Incoming copy and work/review files; never leave exported intermediates next to the source. Mailbox messages (`_de_*`, `_para_*`) are not assets; leave them.

Before importing reworked 3D art into Unreal (meshes split, materials, holograms...), show the owner close-up renders and wait for approval.

**Why:** 2026-11-12, Entity (Tripo #26): I split and imported without asking; the owner found leftover tentacle bases (~5%) stuck on the body and said I should have asked first.

**How to apply:** render each part close up (e.g. each tentacle root individually), send them, ask; import only after the owner says yes. Related: [[assets-move-into-project]].

For first-person weapons, include renders from the player's camera. Owner, 2026-11-12, rifle: that viewpoint "is the right one because it is the one the player will have"; they judged shapes and stains from it over four rounds of notes.

The render must show what the game will show. Same day: my review render drew the additive ammo hologram as an opaque rectangle, and the owner asked to make it "more holographic", judging something the game would not have shown. (My reading: mimic the game material in the review render, or say what the render leaves out.)

241	## Sixteenth block: the assault rifle, from one Tripo mesh to a complete weapon
242	Owner's note (translated): "This is the game's assault rifle. I think it's a single mesh, and all the work it needs is ahead of it; you will do it. Animations, the colour change, the ammo panel, everything as you already know: it has to end up as a complete and absolutely functional weapon, with everything a game of this kind needs. Modify it in Blender or Unreal as you like. For code tasks, don't use Muse Spark, use Sonnet."
243	
244	**The source.** The owner's `carabina-roja.zip` held a Tripo GLB. It is one mesh of about 1,000 loose panels and 5,498 triangles, 1.0 m long. It came with a 4096 albedo and a `neon_mask` that marks where it glows.
245	- It had **no magazine** and no separate moving parts.
246	- The architect (Claude Opus 5.5) did the art headless in Blender 5.3.0, without asking. Scripts:
247	  - `Tools/Blender/rifle_import_glb.py`: GLB to `SourceArt/Weapons/Rifle/Rifle.blend`, the one source;
248	  - `rifle_export_fbx.py`;
249	  - `Tools/Jam/Import-Rifle.ps1` and `import_rifle.py`, with the same one-source rule as the pistol.
250	
251	**The parts and how each was chosen.** The rifle has five meshes in `/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/Rifle`.
252	- **Trigger:** the blade's panels, picked by their bounding box inside the guard. Its origin is at the hinge, so it rotates -8° like the pistol's.
253	- **Magazine:** new geometry modelled by script, because the model had none and a rifle needs one to reload.
254	  - A curved box under the stub in front of the trigger guard, with a base plate.
255	  - A glowing slit on each side, in the element colour.
256	  - On reload it slides out 17 cm, then back in.
257	- **Weak-point light:** the two oval lenses on the sides of the sight. They are off normally and flash on a head or weak-point hit, the pistol's rule.
258	- **Ammo display:** a 2:1 hologram pane just behind the sight's eyepiece, facing the player. It is the pistol's shared `M_GunHolo`, with its own text layout: no frame or dots to avoid, so the number is larger.
259	- **Energy bar:** no separate mesh. The body's second UV map carries the position along the side neon strip, and `M_RifleAtlas` cuts the strip into 13 cells with thin dark gaps.
260	  - They drain from the muzzle end with the enchant's time left: the same "+ half a cell" rule and the same code as the pistol.
261	  - The rest of the neon glows in the element colour all the time: idle mint (the model's own colour), or the enchant's element.
262	- **Problems found by the import checks:**
263	  - The FBX import flips V, so the "on the strip" flag in UV 1 came out inverted. The check that counts strip vertices caught it.
264	  - The magazine's three material slots collapsed into one. A new check now requires 3 slots.
265	  - Both were fixed in the export script before any code used them.
266	- **Textures:** the 4096 maps are capped at 2048 in Unreal.
267	
268	**Code: Claude Sonnet 5.5 at High effort.** The owner set it as the implementer for this chat, so not Muse Spark. Brief: `Prompts/feedback12_rifle_viewmodel.md`.
269	- The pistol-only viewmodel code became one code path for both guns. A small art description per model (folder, parts, offsets, scale, idle glow, muzzle tip, display layout) is chosen by `ViewModel` in `Weapons.json`.
270	- New for both guns:
271	  - **Shot kick:** the viewmodel moves back and tips up, then eases back over 0.09 s. It is the look only; aim and camera are untouched.
272	  - **Muzzle flash:** a 0.05 s glowing star at the muzzle in the glow colour.
273	- The rifle sits at scale 0.62, tuned by Sonnet over several smoke screenshots.
274	- The smoke run has new rifle steps, all green:
275	  - `meshes=5`;
276	  - display `30` → `29` → `--`;
277	  - magazine out 17.1 cm;
278	  - weak-point flash 1.00 → 0.00, and 0.00 on a body shot;
279	  - half bar 0.52;
280	  - muzzle flash and kick on both guns.
281	  - Every pistol line is unchanged.
282	- One deviation, reported by Sonnet: the smoke run applies the rifle's enchant as a status directly, because the enchant spell is still on cooldown from the pistol step.
283	- The architect looked at the screenshots: the rifle is in the lower right, the number reads upright, and the flash sits at the muzzle. Accepted.
284	- **Owner, after the screenshot (translated):** "The rifle closer to the screen", then "the front pointing at the crosshair, a little closer and to the left". Done directly by the architect, because these are values in the rifle's art description:
285	  - root offset (30, 2, 1) → (14, 2, 1) → (8, -3, 2) cm;
286	  - yaw -5° → -10°;
287	  - checked on `media/2026-11-12/14b_rifle_hip_closer.png`: the barrel now runs to the crosshair, and "30" is about twice as large.
288	- Package `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`: 252.8 MB.
289	- **Owner, second note (translated):** "The weapon is still too far away in the frame, bring it closer. Its alignment doesn't go straight to the crosshair: look at how rifles are framed in first-person shooters and adjust it. And look closely at the screenshots you sent: there are still imperfections on the rifle; find them and fix them."
290	  - **Framing.** The architect searched the web: Unreal answers, Leadwerks and Roblox developer threads, and CS2 viewmodel guides. At the hip, the weapon is held parallel to the view, or turned slightly towards the point the crosshair aims at. Perspective then makes the barrel converge on the screen centre. Our -10° yaw made the barrel cross the crosshair instead.
291	    - The rifle is now parallel to the view (yaw -0.4°, the angle that meets the crosshair at 15 m), 20 cm closer and 3 cm further left: root offset (-12, -6, 2) cm.
292	    - The barrel line now runs into the crosshair, and the sight with its ammo count sits in the lower right.
293	  - **Imperfections the architect found on enlarged crops of the screenshots, and the fixes:**
294	    1. The hologram pane spanned the whole sight 4 cm behind its main face. From the first-person camera it stuck out past the sight. It is now inside the rear face of the eyepiece, 1.5 mm in front of it.
295	    2. Right after the rifle was equipped it looked flat, blurry and tan: textures still streaming in at their lowest mip. The two rifle textures are now never streamed (about 5 MB resident).
296	    3. The 10 cm near plane cut the stock open at the bottom right. It is now 3 cm (`DefaultEngine.ini`, `NearClipPlane`), the usual fix for first-person weapons.
297	    4. The white polymer read washed out next to the pistol: albedo × 0.8.
298	  - **Tried and reverted:** a two-sided material, to guard against holes in the loose-panel mesh. The Tripo panels are doubled back to back and z-fought, so the whole rifle looked grainy. It stays one-sided, with the reason written in `import_rifle.py`.
299	  - Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/14c_rifle_hip_framed.png` (idle) and `14d_rifle_enchanted.png` (lightning enchant, half bar).
300	- **Owner, third note (translated):** "In the screenshots you sent, the weapon looks like it's made of jelly." The architect found three causes:
301	  1. **Lost normals.** The Tripo GLB carries custom normals, and the export's bmesh round trip dropped them. Every face was then smooth-shaded, so the hard-surface gun rendered soft and rounded. Fix: edges sharper than 30° are now shaded hard (`set_sharp_from_angle` in `rifle_export_fbx.py`).
302	  2. **One flat material value.** Roughness 0.42 and metallic 0.15 covered the whole gun, so it looked soft and glossy. The source has no roughness map. The albedo's brightness now tells polymer from metal: light parts are matte polymer (roughness 0.68, not metallic), dark parts satin metal (0.36, metallic 0.6).
303	  3. **No self-shadow.** The viewmodel parts cast no shadow at all, so nothing shaded anything else. They are now "self shadow only": the gun shades itself (the sight now drops a shadow on the receiver) but casts nothing on the world. This applies to the pistol too; checked on `13a`, which is unchanged apart from its own shading.
304	  - The rifle textures went back to full 4096 (no streaming), because the parts nearest the camera were blurry at 2048. The package grew from 252.8 to 256 MB.
305	  - **Note on the smoke screenshots:** `14a` comes out tan and grainy whenever the rifle material has just changed. That is the editor's fallback material while shaders compile. The packaged game ships compiled shaders, so it does not happen there.
306	  - Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/14f_rifle_solid.png`, `14g_rifle_solid_enchanted.png`.
307	- **To check by playing:**
308	  - The framing. The stock now goes under the HUD weapon box at the bottom right.
309	  - Whether "30" is readable.
310	  - The look while aiming.
311	  - The feel of full-auto kick.
312	  - The strip draining over a real enchant.
313	
314	## Seventeenth block: the Entity's first model, a metal shell with hologram tentacles
315	The owner sent Tripo variants of one prompt, "un ente mecánico futurista tipo villano…" ("a futuristic mechanical entity, villain type"). First came one zip (variant #53), then `nasry kum.zip`, which held seven more zips.

# Assault rifle (source art)

The source file for the assault rifle ("carabina roja"). The owner handed it over on 2026-11-12 as `carabina-roja.zip`, which held `model.glb` (a Tripo mesh, node `tripo_node_37918fc6`; SHA-256 `46E9206D59D058C79C0553A40A22DBC3571D2B0D9FE53ED628D1C775139A0C34`) and a preview. The zip was not copied into the project.

- **The GLB as it comes:** a low-poly export.
  - 5,498 triangles, split into about 1,000 loose panels, 1.0 m long, muzzle towards -Y, up +Z.
  - One 4096 albedo with baked light, smears and soft edges, and a `neon_mask`. No roughness, metallic, normal or AO map.
  - Top rail teeth of uneven length and spacing.
- **`Rifle.blend` is rebuilt from it** by `Tools/Blender/rifle_build_blend.py` (the first version was the plain GLB import, and the rifle read soft in the game):
  - SHA-256 `E2F459181DDB57C07CE9E0DC09FF4576E61DDBE59C95FCE168D8A4188216AE45` (Blender 5.3.0);
  - vertices welded, Tripo's normals dropped, hard edges above 30°, face-area weighted normals;
  - `T_Rifle_BaseColor`: one flat tone per panel (white polymer, two greys, dark metal) and the small drawn details re-cut crisp; the barrel, front sight, eyepiece and the band beside the rail are forced to dark metal as whole parts, because their panels came out as patches of different tones;
  - `T_Rifle_ORM`: AO baked in Cycles, roughness and metallic by tone;
  - `T_Rifle_Normal`: baked in Cycles (OpenGL): rounded edges and the drawn details pressed in;
  - `T_Rifle_EmissiveMask`: the neon mask with its edges re-cut, and without the GLB's ragged side strip on the handguard;
  - modelled by the script, in the flat metal slot `Rifle_Rail`:
    - the top rail: the old one deleted, 23 equal teeth (10 mm, 6.4 mm gaps), chamfered;
    - a raised white panel over the whole upper sloped face of the handguard on each side (atlas slot): the face has a stair-stepped groove 5 to 8 mm deep, the channel of the GLB's neon, and a metal block fills the notch it leaves in the ledge above;
    - an energy bar on each panel: a dark bezel 238 mm long with a straight glowing strip (the strip uses the atlas slot);
    - the ammo hologram's emitter at the foot of the sight's eyepiece: a low block with a glowing slit (the slit uses the atlas slot);
  - also modelled by the script: the hologram pane (38 × 19 mm, floating over the emitter, tilted 14° up towards the player) and the magazine (the GLB has none: a curved box, base plate and a glowing slit on each side);
  - objects `Rifle_Body`, `Rifle_Trigger`, `Rifle_Lens`, `Rifle_AmmoDisplay`, `Rifle_Magazine`. Pivots, the magazine's slide-out vector and the strip's span are custom properties on them, read by the export.
  - To rebuild: `blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Blender/rifle_build_blend.py -- <model.glb> Rifle.blend` (about 4 minutes, most of it the two bakes).
- **One rifle, one source** (owner's rule): `Rifle.blend` is the only source and `/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/Rifle` the only result. `Tools/Jam/Import-Rifle.ps1` (Editor closed, pistol imported first):
  - exports the five parts and the four textures (`rifle_export_fbx.py`) into a temporary folder under `Saved/`;
  - imports them with their materials (`import_rifle.py`);
  - deletes the folder.
- The parts:
  - body, with the modelled rail, side panels, energy bars and hologram emitter;
  - trigger, picked by the box of its panels, origin at its hinge;
  - magazine, modelled;
  - weak-point light: the two oval lenses of the sight;
  - ammo display: a 2:1 hologram pane floating behind the sight's eyepiece, with its own material `M_RifleHolo`.
- Energy strip: in the body's second UV map (`ImbueU`):
  - U runs from 0 at the muzzle end of the energy bars' strips to 1 at their rear end;
  - in Blender, V = 1 on the strip and 0 off it, flipped by the import;
  - `M_RifleAtlas` cuts the strip into 13 cells that drain like the pistol's bar.
- `export_report.json` is written by each import: the offsets and motion the game code uses (`AGBGun`).

bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.20, 0.22, 0.26, 1)

sc.world = world
for ob in list(bpy.data.objects):

    def holo_material(name, ink):
        """Emission added over what is behind. Object coordinates: X right, Y up, origin at the pane's centre."""
        hm = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
        hm.use_nodes = True
        nt = hm.node_tree
        nt.nodes.clear()

        def math(op, x, y=None):
            n = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMath")
            n.operation = op
            for i, val in enumerate((x, y)):
                if val is None:
                    continue
                if isinstance(val, (int, float)):
                    n.inputs[i].default_value = val
                else:
                    nt.links.new(val, n.inputs[i])
            return n.outputs[0]

        xyz = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ")
        nt.links.new(coord.outputs["Object"], xyz.inputs["Vector"])

        v = math("SUBTRACT", 0.5, math("DIVIDE", xyz.outputs["Y"], height))    # 0 top .. 1 foot
        scan = math("ADD", math("MULTIPLY", math("SINE", math("MULTIPLY", v, SCANLINES * 6.2831853)), SCAN_DEPTH / 2.0),
                    1.0 - SCAN_DEPTH / 2.0)

        def inset(c, gain):
            near = math("MINIMUM", c, math("SUBTRACT", 1.0, c))
            n = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeClamp")
            nt.links.new(math("MULTIPLY", near, gain), n.inputs["Value"])
            return n.outputs[0]

        edge = math("MULTIPLY", inset(u, EDGE[0]), inset(v, EDGE[1]))
        level = ink if ink is not None else math("MULTIPLY", math("ADD", math("MULTIPLY", v, 1.2), 0.4), TINT)

# after welding vertices, open edges, materials, images and UV maps. Read-only: nothing is saved.
# Usage: blender -b --factory-startup --python shotgun_inspect.py -- <model.fbx> [weld_mm]
import bpy, bmesh, sys, os, glob
from mathutils import Vector

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
fbx = argv[0]
weld = (float(argv[1]) if len(argv) > 1 else 0.01) / 1000.0
bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
bpy.ops.import_scene.fbx(filepath=fbx)
print("BLENDER", bpy.app.version_string)

for im in bpy.data.images:
    if im.size[0] == 0:
        hits = glob.glob(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(fbx), "*.fbm", "*"))
        print("IMAGE_UNRESOLVED", im.name, im.filepath, "candidates", [os.path.basename(h) for h in hits])
        if len(hits) == 1:
            im.filepath = hits[0]
            im.reload()
    print("IMAGE", im.name, tuple(im.size), im.colorspace_settings.name, im.filepath)

for ob in bpy.data.objects:
    print("OBJECT", ob.name, ob.type, "parent", ob.parent.name if ob.parent else "-",
          "loc", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in ob.location), "rot", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in ob.rotation_euler),
          "scale", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in ob.scale), "dims", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in ob.dimensions))

for m in bpy.data.materials:
    print("MATERIAL", m.name)
    if m.use_nodes:
        for n in m.node_tree.nodes:
            print("   node", n.bl_idname, n.name, getattr(getattr(n, "image", None), "name", ""))
        for l in m.node_tree.links:
            print("   link", l.from_node.name, l.from_socket.identifier, "->", l.to_node.name, l.to_socket.identifier)
        b = m.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
        if b:
            for k in ("Metallic", "Roughness"):
                print("   ", k, b.inputs[k].default_value, "linked" if b.inputs[k].is_linked else "")


def islands(bm):
    seen, out = set(), []
    for v in bm.verts:
        if v.index in seen:
            continue
        stack, verts = [v], []
        seen.add(v.index)
        while stack:
            a = stack.pop()
            verts.append(a)
            for e in a.link_edges:
                b = e.other_vert(a)
                if b.index not in seen:
                    seen.add(b.index)
                    stack.append(b)
        out.append(verts)
    return out


for ob in [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"]:
    me = ob.data
    print("MESH", ob.name, "verts", len(me.vertices), "polys", len(me.polygons),
          "tris", sum(len(p.vertices) - 2 for p in me.polygons),
          "uv", [u.name for u in me.uv_layers], "colors", [c.name for c in me.color_attributes],
          "custom_normals", me.has_custom_normals, "slots", [s.material.name if s.material else "-" for s in ob.material_slots])
    mw = ob.matrix_world
    pts = [mw @ v.co for v in me.vertices]
    lo = Vector([min(p[i] for p in pts) for i in range(3)])
    hi = Vector([max(p[i] for p in pts) for i in range(3)])
    print("  WORLD_BOUNDS min", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in lo), "max", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in hi),
          "size", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in hi - lo))
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(me)
    bm.transform(mw)
    bm.verts.index_update()
    print("  LOOSE_PIECES_AS_IS", len(islands(bm)), "open_edges", sum(1 for e in bm.edges if e.is_boundary))
    bmesh.ops.remove_doubles(bm, verts=bm.verts, dist=weld)
    bm.verts.index_update()
    isl = islands(bm)
    print("  AFTER_WELD_%gmm" % (weld * 1000), "verts", len(bm.verts), "pieces", len(isl),
          "open_edges", sum(1 for e in bm.edges if e.is_boundary),
          "non_manifold", sum(1 for e in bm.edges if not e.is_manifold and not e.is_boundary))
    isl.sort(key=lambda vs: -len(vs))
    for i, vs in enumerate(isl[:40]):
        a = Vector([min(v.co[k] for v in vs) for k in range(3)])
        b = Vector([max(v.co[k] for v in vs) for k in range(3)])
        faces = {f.index for v in vs for f in v.link_faces}
        print("   PIECE %d verts %d faces %d min %s max %s" % (i, len(vs), len(faces),
              tuple(round(v, 3) for v in a), tuple(round(v, 3) for v in b)))
    bm.free()

# Headless inventory of the shotgun's Tripo FBX as it comes: objects, size, axes, triangles, loose pieces before and
# after welding vertices, open edges, materials, images and UV maps. Read-only: nothing is saved.
# Usage: blender -b --factory-startup --python shotgun_inspect.py -- <model.fbx> [weld_mm]
import bpy, bmesh, sys, os, glob
from mathutils import Vector

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
fbx = argv[0]
weld = (float(argv[1]) if len(argv) > 1 else 0.01) / 1000.0
bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
bpy.ops.import_scene.fbx(filepath=fbx)
print("BLENDER", bpy.app.version_string)

for im in bpy.data.images:
    if im.size[0] == 0:
        hits = glob.glob(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(fbx), "*.fbm", "*"))
        print("IMAGE_UNRESOLVED", im.name, im.filepath, "candidates", [os.path.basename(h) for h in hits])
        if len(hits) == 1:
            im.filepath = hits[0]
            im.reload()
    print("IMAGE", im.name, tuple(im.size), im.colorspace_settings.name, im.filepath)

for ob in bpy.data.objects:
    print("OBJECT", ob.name, ob.type, "parent", ob.parent.name if ob.parent else "-",
          "loc", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in ob.location), "rot", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in ob.rotation_euler),
          "scale", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in ob.scale), "dims", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in ob.dimensions))

for m in bpy.data.materials:
    print("MATERIAL", m.name)
    if m.use_nodes:
        for n in m.node_tree.nodes:
            print("   node", n.bl_idname, n.name, getattr(getattr(n, "image", None), "name", ""))
        for l in m.node_tree.links:
            print("   link", l.from_node.name, l.from_socket.identifier, "->", l.to_node.name, l.to_socket.identifier)
        b = m.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
        if b:
            for k in ("Metallic", "Roughness"):
                print("   ", k, b.inputs[k].default_value, "linked" if b.inputs[k].is_linked else "")


def islands(bm):
    seen, out = set(), []
    for v in bm.verts:
        if v.index in seen:
            continue
        stack, verts = [v], []
        seen.add(v.index)
        while stack:
            a = stack.pop()
            verts.append(a)
            for e in a.link_edges:
                b = e.other_vert(a)
                if b.index not in seen:
                    seen.add(b.index)
                    stack.append(b)
        out.append(verts)
    return out


for ob in [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"]:
    me = ob.data
    print("MESH", ob.name, "verts", len(me.vertices), "polys", len(me.polygons),
          "tris", sum(len(p.vertices) - 2 for p in me.polygons),
          "uv", [u.name for u in me.uv_layers], "colors", [c.name for c in me.color_attributes],
          "custom_normals", me.has_custom_normals, "slots", [s.material.name if s.material else "-" for s in ob.material_slots])
    mw = ob.matrix_world
    pts = [mw @ v.co for v in me.vertices]
    lo = Vector([min(p[i] for p in pts) for i in range(3)])
    hi = Vector([max(p[i] for p in pts) for i in range(3)])
    print("  WORLD_BOUNDS min", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in lo), "max", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in hi),
          "size", tuple(round(v, 4) for v in hi - lo))
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(me)
    bm.transform(mw)
    bm.verts.index_update()
    print("  LOOSE_PIECES_AS_IS", len(islands(bm)), "open_edges", sum(1 for e in bm.edges if e.is_boundary))
    bmesh.ops.remove_doubles(bm, verts=bm.verts, dist=weld)
    bm.verts.index_update()
    isl = islands(bm)
    print("  AFTER_WELD_%gmm" % (weld * 1000), "verts", len(bm.verts), "pieces", len(isl),
          "open_edges", sum(1 for e in bm.edges if e.is_boundary),
          "non_manifold", sum(1 for e in bm.edges if not e.is_manifold and not e.is_boundary))
    isl.sort(key=lambda vs: -len(vs))
    for i, vs in enumerate(isl[:40]):
        a = Vector([min(v.co[k] for v in vs) for k in range(3)])
        b = Vector([max(v.co[k] for v in vs) for k in range(3)])
        faces = {f.index for v in vs for f in v.link_faces}
        print("   PIECE %d verts %d faces %d min %s max %s" % (i, len(vs), len(faces),
              tuple(round(v, 3) for v in a), tuple(round(v, 3) for v in b)))
    bm.free()
